newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures drop on Chicago, weather.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures drop on Chicago, weather.

text.p: Lower Chicago prices and good weather pushed most grains futures lower on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Friday in heavy turnover, traders said.
"Strangely enough, as prices went down, producers seemed to be more willing to sell," said Mihaly Otvos of brokerage OTP Forex.
He added that with the improved weather and good crop forecasts producers were more confident of the future and had decided to sell stocks.
Milling wheat futures dropped by the daily allowed 400-forint per tonne limit for the nearest contracts and by 180 to 370 forints for all other maturities.
"At the moment, the wheat crop looks like it is going to hit a five-year record," Otvos said.
Milling wheat futures accounted for 1,371 lots of a considerable turnover of 2,468 lots.
Maize futures also dropped for most maturities by between 50 and 400 forints except for October which bucked the trend rising 290 forints to 20,000.
Even so, a negative spread remains between October and July maize, which dropped 50 forints to 20,250.
